sign verb

put one’s name to

also signature, sign here, sign a document, sign a contract, autograph

classical

Traupman 379
M-O s.v. sign vb.: subscrībere (alicui reī); testāmentō subscrībere (Dig. 40.7.40)

subscrībō, subscrībere, subscrīpsī, subscrīptum

verb, third conjugation, with the dative of what is signed

sign (write one’s name under)

Classically to write underneath: a caption under a statue (Cic. Clu. 101), one’s name under an accusation or a will (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • subscrīptiō, subscrīptiōnis f. — signature; what is written underneath

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 6.1.17 (Lewis & Short)

  • obsignō, obsignāre, obsignāvī, obsignātum — seal (a letter, a will)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 748 (Lewis & Short: obsignā cito); Comen. OP 98: Epistula complicātur, īnscrībitur, et obsignātur.

    Romans sealed a document with a ring rather than signing it.

Examples

  • Hīc subscrībe.

    Sign here.composed

See also sign, pen.

SourcesLewis & Short: subscribo · Lewis & Short: subscriptio · Lewis & Short: obsigno
